verdicts.load: St. Lawrence Infrastructure 2 (St. Lawrence Infrastructure LLC, 1,935 MW)
verdicts.reason: Core claim verified against the live NYISO queue workbook (Load Projects sheet, queue 1743): POI reads verbatim "NYPA's 230kV Moses Massena 1 (MMS-1) and 230kV Moses Massena 2 (MMS-2)"; 1,935 MW, St. Lawrence County, Zone D, CTO/Utility NYPA, ATO column blank — all as claimed, and interconnection.fyi/project/nyiso-1743 shows the same POI text. 'Dual named circuits at the POI' stands. TWO CORRECTIONS to the detail, however. (1) The 'no second substation / dual-circuit, single-substation service' gloss is NOT supported and is contradicted by NYISO's own Moses South stability report (MS-24, OC-approved 7/18/2024, nyiso.com): MMS1/MMS2 are the 230 kV circuits BETWEEN the Moses 230 kV switchyard and the Massena 765/230 kV substation (contingencies are modeled at both @MOSES230 and @MASSENA765 ends, e.g. 'L/O MASSENA-MOSES 765/230 MMS1'), and Massena is a second, independently sourced major substation — the Massena–Marcy 765 kV line (MSU1) and the 765 kV Chateauguay HVDC interconnection with Hydro-Quebec terminate there. The queue record is silent on which end (or a mid-line tap) serves the load, so 'single-substation service' is an inference the record does not support; the circuit names themselves name a second substation (Massena). (2) The dual-circuit redundancy is weaker than the claim implies in a different way: NYISO contingency NYPA13 models loss of MMS1 & MMS2 together as a single 'DCT' (double-circuit tower) event, i.e. the two named circuits share towers for at least part of the route, so they are not fully independent feeds. Suggested rewrite: 'dual named circuits on a shared double-circuit-tower line between two NYPA substations (Moses 230 kV switchyard and Massena 765/230 kV); queue names no serving substation.'

findings.load: Micron Clay megafab (NYISO phases 576 MW + 480 MW)
findings.detail: Documented plan is a large fleet of diesel emergency generators. Times Union (2026): 'Budget bill would exempt Micron from permit for backup diesel power' — reports Micron plans 118 diesel-powered backup generators for the megafab, and that the Hochul administration inserted state-budget language waiving Article 10 siting review (which applies at 25 MW+ of generation, implying the backup fleet exceeds 25 MW in aggregate) specifically for 'emergency backup generation' at Green CHIPS semiconductor sites; the article also says Micron evaluated natural-gas combustion turbines, dual-fired engines, and fuel cells but settled on diesel as most reliable. (Article is paywalled; the 118-generator figure comes from its search snippet, corroborated consistently across two independent searches, so treat the exact count as medium confidence within an otherwise high-confidence diesel finding.) Primary regulatory corroboration: NYSDEC CLCPA Section 7(2) justification statement (Dec 12, 2025) lists Micron's 'acceptance of operational restrictions on emergency engine use at the facility (78,837 metric tons CO2e per year reduction)' and limits on 'boilers, water bath vaporizers, and stationary emergency engines'; NYSDEC's Air Title V justification (Mar 31, 2026) confirms the final Title V air permit issued 3/31/2026 carries those emergency-engine restrictions as enforceable conditions. A diesel-fired emergency fire pump engine is also permitted. Scale of the load being backed up: regulatory filings cited in trade coverage put full-buildout site demand at 1.8 GW.

findings.detail: The only documented point of interconnection is a tap of the NYPA Clay-Pannell 345 kV circuits PC-1 and PC-2 (interconnection.fyi's NYISO queue tracking: applied 5/7/2025, 300 MW, NYPA as connecting utility, expected in-service 05-2028). research.cluster_note: Both loads are single-corridor dependents of National Grid's Clay 345kV substation, making it a common-mode failure point for the cluster. Micron's entire permitted supply (eight 345kV underground laterals to four fabs; full-buildout demand cited at 1.8 GW) originates at the expanded Clay Substation; Ranalli SuperDC's documented POI is a tap of the NYPA Clay-Pannell 345kV circuits PC-1/PC-2, which leave that same substation. A Clay substation outage would interrupt grid supply to both loads simultaneously; a Clay-Pannell corridor loss would hit Ranalli and degrade the network around Micron. On backup: Micron has a well-documented diesel emergency fleet (reported 118 gensets, aggregate >25 MW since an Article 10 siting waiver was legislated for it; emergency-engine operational restrictions are enforceable conditions in the Title V air permit issued 3/31/2026), sized for tool-protection ride-through rather than continued operation. Ranalli has no documented backup plan at all — the project has no town planning application yet and faces a drafted Lysander data-center moratorium, so its resilience posture is unknowable from the public record at this date. Caveats: the Micron 118-generator count is sourced from a paywalled Times Union article via consistent search snippets; the Ranalli MW figure in sources (300 MW) differs from the task premise (270 MW); and Ranalli parcels sit in Lysander on the Clay-Pannell line rather than at the Clay substation fence, so its electrical distance from the Clay bus is nonzero but the corridor dependency stands.
